saturation_history.rationale: All provided open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) maps provider facade → Dimension 6 (External Map Provider Integration via Facade); (2) repository abstraction for orders/promotions/subscriptions → Dimension 5 (Repository-Based Data Access Abstraction by Domain); (3) encrypted credential storage + strict access controls + standard credential verification → Dimension 1 (Authentication Credential Verification and Storage Security); (4) meal search filtering using specification pattern + explicit availability/dietary criteria → Dimension 4 (Meal Search and Filtering Composition Strategy); (5) multi-step registration with confirmation + input validation → Dimension 2 (User Registration Onboarding Workflow Structure); (6) MVC for core user interaction flows (including order history/promotions/subscriptions) → Dimension 3 (User Interface Interaction Pattern for Core Flows). Since each open code aligns with an existing dimension’s axis of variation (and thus can be absorbed without conflating different architectural concerns), the taxonomy is theoretically saturated for this minibatch.

All open codes are already directly covered by existing taxonomy dimensions:
- Observer pattern for promotion/subscription plan change propagation + synchronizing frontend UI with plan-change events are both covered by dimension 8 (Promotion and Subscription Plan Change Propagation) values 8.1 and 8.2.
- Adapter pattern for multi–map-provider integration and Strategy pattern for runtime swapping of map providers and search algorithms are covered by dimensions 6 and 7 respectively (values 6.2 and 7.1).
- The repository-design codes (user-profile, meal-order, meal-catalog) and “use repository pattern as the abstraction layer for core domain data access” are all covered by dimension 5 (Repository-Based Data Access Abstraction by Domain) values 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, and 5.5.
Therefore, no relevant uncovered concepts remain.
